description: We are Team B-612, tackling NASA'a "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer". Inspired by exploration, we are building a web-based mission survival simulator where players become commanders of a lunar/Martian outpost.They must balance power, life support, radiation, shielding, and food within strict payload limits. Using modern web technology, we turn real-world aerospace engineering and learning experience for young explorers.
summary:
Mysha Goes to Mars is a free, browser-based 3D game for kids aged 7 to 12 that lets them feel the trade-offs of surviving on Mars. Players guide Mysha through four levels: mission preparation, a deep-space oxygen emergency, a Mars landing where 100 mission points must be split between competing needs, and survival at a Mars base. They balance food, water, power, life support, radiation protection and return-rocket readiness, and every choice has a cost. Before confirming an action, players see its effects and a NASA research note explaining the real science. Each run ends with one of four outcomes and a debrief, followed by a Mars Discovery Archive linking to NASA resources. Game meters are labelled as educational simplifications, while the science panels reference NASA-STD-3001, NASA ECLSS, MSL RAD, MEDA and JPL Mars 2020. No download or account is needed.
Play it at https://mysha-goes-to-mars.vercel.app
details:
THE CHALLENGE

Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: space STEM content for kids is often too simple to show real engineering trade-offs, or too complex to hold a young learner's attention. Our game lets kids run a Mars mission and feel those trade-offs by playing.

WHAT WE BUILT

Mysha Goes to Mars is a story-driven 3D browser game. The player guides Mysha through:

  • Level 1, Mission Preparation: Explore the facility, check supplies and prepare for launch.
  • Level 2, Journey Through Space: handle an oxygen and life-support emergency.
  • Level 3, Mars Landing: split 100 mission points across competing priorities (for example, more water means less radiation shielding). The choice carries into Level 4.
  • Level 4, Life on Mars: visit six stations (habitat, hydroponics, water recycling, radiation shelter, solar power, return rocket), review the effects of each action before confirming, survive a solar and dust crisis and try to board the return rocket.

There are four possible outcomes: Mission Successful, Partial Success, Mission Compromised and Mission Failed. No choice is free. A debrief explains what happened, and the Mars Discovery Archive explains the science with links to NASA resources.

HOW NASA DATA AND RESEARCH ARE USED

- NASA-STD-3001: crew health and safety context.

- NASA ECLSS: life-support and water-recovery context.

- MSL RAD (Curiosity): radiation education and hazard explanation.

- MEDA (Perseverance): Mars weather and dust context.

- JPL Mars 2020 landing: landing story and terminology.

WHY IT MATTERS / BENEFITS

  • Plays in a browser, no download or account.
  • Teaches cause and effect: every decision has an immediate and a later cost.
  • Replayable: Four outcomes encourage kids to try new strategies and learn from failure.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Vitest, ESLint, Prettier, Git and GitHub, deployed on Vercel.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) USE

  • Code: ChatGPT, Claude and VS Code coding agent helped draft, debug and refactor code. We reviewed, tested and edited it.
  • Design: Lovable was used for visual prototyping.
  • video: Gemini was used to generate the cinematic video clips.
  • Character: 3D character created from Sketchfab.
  • No AI model runs while the game is played, and the game makes no API calls.
  • Game design, story, balancing, UI, testing and deployment were done by our team.
  • Prompts and workflow: https://github.com/Shihab-10/mysha-goes-to-mars/blob/main/docs/AI_PROMPT_LOG.md
